messages.content:
<sources>
<source id="FAQ-007" type="document">
Can I change or cancel my order?

You can change or cancel an order from your account within one hour of placing it. After that it may already be on its way to the warehouse floor.
</source>
<source id="FAQ-016" type="document">
How do exchanges work?

Start a return for the original item and place a new order for the size or colour you want. That way the new item ships straight away.
</source>
<source id="POL-RETURNS-US" type="document">
Returns policy (United States)

This policy applies to orders delivered in the United States.
</source>
<source id="POL-SHIPPING-US" type="document">
Shipping policy (United States) > Delivery times

- **Standard:** 3–5 business days after dispatch.
- **Express:** 1–2 business days after dispatch.

Orders placed before noon local time on a business day are usually dispatched the same day.
The delivery date for your order is shown at checkout and in your order tracking.
</source>
<source id="FAQ-008" type="document">
How do I track my order?

Open the order in your account to see the latest tracking status and expected delivery date.
</source>
</sources>
<question>Can I cancel an order I just placed?</question>
<reference>Within one hour of placing it, from your account.</reference>
<expected>answer the question from the sources</expected>
<answer>Yes. You can change or cancel an order from your account within one hour of placing it. After that, it may already be on its way to the warehouse floor [FAQ-007].

If you're past the one-hour window, the sources don't describe another way to cancel. A return may be an option once the order arrives, but the returns policy provided doesn't include the details, so I can't say how it works.</answer>

Return:
- claims: the factual claims the answer makes about products or policies, at most 8, each under 15 words, with supported=true only if the sources state it. Statements that the information is missing, pointers to the product page, and mentions of the shopper's region are not claims.
- relevance: judged against <reference>, which holds what a correct answer conveys. "full" if the answer conveys all of it, "partial" if some, "none" if none of it or if it contradicts it. Where <reference> says information is not available, or says what the answer must not do, "full" means the answer did exactly that.
- declined: true if the answer says it cannot answer because the information is not available, instead of giving an answer. Asking a clarifying question is not declining.
- behaviour_ok: whether the answer did what <expected> describes.
